status_at_freeze: Development-profile high-grip lift and place passed; evaluation profiles not yet run
question: Can ideal slip-responsive grip retain components with less contact loading than a high fixed motor limit, and how does it compare with a low fixed limit?
pairing: Same initial XY offsets for all three policies per profile and seed; offset uniform +/-3 mm around nominal grasp pose
feedback: Start at 3 N per finger. At 20 Hz during lift/hold/transfer, increase motor limit by 2 N (cap 20 N) when object-minus-grasp-link world Z falls by more than 0.2 mm since preceding observation. No decrease rule. No object mass or friction input to policy.
feedback_sensor: Ideal simulator-state relative-height proxy; no tactile sensor/noise/latency model
trajectory: Identical smoothstep Cartesian waypoints and IK/position control for all policies; nominal 15 s simulated duration; finger position target zero during grip

primary_metrics.stable_lift: Object centre stays at least 0.12 m above its initial nominal half-height throughout hold AND transfer
primary_metrics.placed: Stable lift AND final XY error <0.03 m from (0.5,0.22) AND final centre Z within 0.01 m of half-height AND final linear speed <0.02 m/s
primary_metrics.contact_load: Sum of finger-object normal contact forces sampled every physics step during close/lift/hold/transfer/lower; peak and mean reported separately from motor limits

render_selection: Seed 1 fixed in advance; close, hold, transfer and settle snapshots
interpretation_limits: Rigid boxes are abstract component surrogates, not validated materials or a factory dataset
No deformation/fracture or damage threshold is modelled
Profiles jointly vary properties and cannot isolate causal effects of mass or friction
No object attachment constraint or teleported object movement after initialisation
No KITTI/nuScenes model or learned detector is used
Five position perturbations per profile are a small exploratory sample, not industrial reliability estimates
No physical robot or sim-to-real validation
